items.title: Tune identity and enumeration
items.text: This reference describes the implemented tune codec in nmr/types/tune.py and its rational counting functions in nmr/types/tune_count.py. Usage, browser controls, and operational bounds are documented in README.md.

items.title: Musical identity
items.text:
The codec combines melody and rhythm using successive semitone differences and exact beat durations. The first relative pitch is zero internally; presentation can transpose the phrase without changing its identity.

  • A tune is a nonempty, finite, monophonic sequence of attacked notes. Chords and overlapping notes are outside this profile.
  • Store each pitch after the first as a signed interval from the previous sounding note. Do not store note letters or a key signature in the identity.
  • Use integer semitone differences in twelve-tone equal temperament. Preserve direction and octave distances; do not reduce intervals modulo twelve. Microtonal grids would require a separately allocated profile, not a local setting that changes the meaning of existing truenames.
  • The first relative pitch is implicitly zero. Presentation centers the sequence around a configurable root using the rule below. The Python API defaults to C4; the browser defaults to F3. Changing the presentation root or transposing every input pitch equally does not change the truename. The first sounding note need not be C.
  • There is no inferred scale or tonic. Centering on C does not make the tune C major. Chromatic intervals remain available.
  • Each note has an exact positive duration in beats. Each later note also has an exact nonnegative gap after the preceding note ends.
  • Playback tempo, timbre, velocity, written enharmonic spelling, meter, barlines, and beaming are presentation choices, not encoded identity.
  • The beat remains a reference unit. Doubling every encoded beat duration gives a different rhythm; changing playback BPM alone does not. Do not silently normalize the first duration to one. Full proportional-rhythm equivalence would be a different identity decision.
  • Leading and trailing silence are outside the encoded phrase. Remove them from keyboard or imported performance input before producing interval notation, and show that normalization before encoding. Interval text itself must start with @, never a rest or offset. Reject an empty or all-rest input.
  • Merge adjacent rests into one intervening gap. Tied notes form one sustained note. Two attacks at the same pitch remain two notes, even with no gap.
  • A rest does not reset the pitch reference: the next interval is measured from the previous sounding note.

These rules truename an abstract musical phrase, not a performance or score file. There is no requirement that a generated tune be pleasant or recognizable.

items.title: What divisions by two and three mean
items.text:
Interpret this as rhythmic subdivision of a beat. Every duration or positive gap must be a rational number whose reduced denominator has no prime factors other than two and three, and at most one factor of three:

d = u / (2^a * 3^b)
u >= 1; a >= 0; b in {0, 1}

The fraction must be reduced: if a > 0, u is odd; if b > 0, u is not divisible by three. There is no restriction that the numerator itself contain only factors two and three.

Examples include 1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/6, 1/8, 1/12, 2/3, 3/2, and 7/4. This covers arbitrary binary subdivisions, triplets, and binary subdivisions of triplets, but excludes nested triplets such as 1/9 and 1/18. Adding or tying allowed durations always produces another allowed duration. A five-beat note is allowed; one fifth of a beat is not. A quarter note split into three equal parts is allowed.

Reduce fractions before validation. Thus 2/6 and 3/9 mean 1/3, while 1/5 and 1/9 are rejected. Exact decimal input is converted to a rational value; it must satisfy the same denominator restriction. Approximate decimals are never rounded to triplets. Use fractions.Fraction internally; duration equivalence differs deliberately from nmr's pair-preserving Frac type.

Keep exact beat durations rather than dividing every duration by the first one: scaling a five-beat first note to one could turn a later one-beat note into the unsupported duration 1/5. Ignoring playback BPM does not require changing the encoded beat reference.

items.title: Canonical input and output
items.text:
Provide a compact interval-and-duration notation. For example:

@1 2@1/2 2@1/2 r@1/3 -1@2/3 @1

This means an initial note lasting one beat, two successive upward semitone-pair steps lasting half a beat each, a one-third-beat rest, a downward semitone step lasting two thirds, and a repeated attack at that pitch lasting one beat.

The first token is @duration: a phrase must start with @, with no initial offset, even an explicit zero. Later note tokens are step@duration, with no + on positive steps. A later zero step may be written 0@duration or @duration; canonical output always omits the zero. Rest tokens use r@duration. Durations print as reduced fractions, or integers when their denominator is one. Canonical output has one space between tokens, with no edge rests or adjacent rest tokens. Same-pitch attacks are never merged automatically.

The UI may accept absolute pitches through a keyboard or note editor, then convert them to successive differences and discard the initial absolute pitch. Show the normalized phrase and allow playback before encoding. The core numeric notation does not need note truenames to represent the melody.

items.title: Presentation centering
items.text:
Center the cumulative sounding pitches, not the written intervals. Recover relative pitches from the interval sequence as follows:

p1 = 0
pi = p(i-1) + step_i
S = sum(pi)
mean = S / m

Use the arithmetic mean over the m attacked notes, counting repeated notes separately. Rests do not contribute, and note durations do not weight the mean. Round to the nearest semitone, with exact half-semitone ties away from zero. For example, 0.4 rounds to 0, 0.6 to 1, -0.6 to -1, and +/-0.5 to +/-1. Compute the rounded center k using exact integer arithmetic:

k = sign(S) * floor((2*abs(S) + m) / (2*m))

With configured root pitch R, present each note at:

presented_pitch_i = R + pi - k

For the example phrase, the intervals are 0, 2, 2, -1, 0, while the cumulative pitches are 0, 2, 4, 3, 3. Their mean is 12/5 = 2.4, so k = 2. The presented offsets from the configured root are -2, 0, 2, 1, 1. With C4 as the root, these sound as Bb3, C4, D4, Db4, Db4, using one possible enharmonic spelling. Averaging the intervals instead would yield 0.6; that is not the centering rule.

Use the same placement for playback and absolute-pitch displays. The exact arithmetic mean can remain within half a semitone of the configured root because the placement shifts by whole semitones. Changing the root transposes the entire presentation; it must not change the interval text, ranking, or canonical truename. Centering is a presentation transform, not a step in the integer enumeration.

items.title: A dense duration enumeration
items.text:
Do not independently pack (u, a, b) and then reduce the fraction. That would assign several integers to the same duration, defeating invertibility.

Instead enumerate only reduced durations, in finite complexity layers. Set h = floor(log2(u)), computed using integer bit length, and define:

weight = 4*h + a + 3*b

The numerator bit-length costs four per step, delaying long durations. Binary subdivision costs one per step. The optional factor of three costs three, so thirds arrive modestly later; further factors of three are excluded. These weights define the enumeration, not playback settings; changing them changes truenames. This favors short binary durations, including very short ones, so assess the musical balance through playback during implementation.

Visit weights in ascending order. Within a weight, visit h in ascending order, then b in ascending order over {0, 1}; a = weight - 4*h - 3*b is determined. Visit h <= floor(weight/4) and omit groups with a < 0. For each group, visit permitted numerators u in ascending order in:

2^h <= u < 2^(h+1)

Omit numerators divisible by two when a > 0, and by three when b > 0. Assign consecutive duration indices D(d), starting at zero. The beginning is:

Index Duration in beats 0 1 1 ½ 2 ¼ 3 ⅛ 4 ⅓ 5 1/16 6 ⅙ 7 2 8 3 9 1/32 10 1/12 11 3/2

Compared with the unweighted h + a + b ordering, two beats move from index 3 to 7, four beats from 10 to 22, and thirds from 2 to 4. Ninths are excluded.

Every allowed positive duration appears exactly once: reduced numerator and denominator exponents are unique, and they determine exactly one group. Every group is finite, and every weight has entries (1/2^weight is always present). Thus all nonnegative duration indices have inverses without aliases or holes.

Rank and unrank by counting groups, not by visiting every numerator. For a group with inclusive numerator bounds L and U, let:

multiples(k) = floor(U/k) - floor((L-1)/k)

Its size is U-L+1, subtracting multiples(2) if needed and multiples(3) if needed, then adding back multiples(6) if both restrictions apply. The same counting function on a prefix of [L,U] permits binary-search unranking of the numerator. Cache or derive exact layer/group prefix counts for larger weights.

This ordering also avoids an important computational trap: directly packing unbounded denominator exponents can make a short integer demand a denominator with an astronomically large number of digits. Here, for w >= 1, weight w has at least 2^ceil(w/4)-1 preceding entries from integer durations alone. For duration index r, this gives w <= 4*floor(log2(r+1)); index zero has weight zero. Also a <= w, b <= 1, and h <= floor(w/4). Consequently denominator exponents and numerator bit-length remain bounded by the duration index's bit-length, not its numeric value. Construct fractions only after checking work estimates.

items.title: Encode melody and rhythm together
items.text:
Enumerate complete tunes by total musical complexity. Each attack costs one; steps from -2 through +2 semitones have no extra cost, and larger steps cost abs(step)-2; durations retain weight 4*h+a+3*b; a positive gap costs one plus its duration weight. No gap costs zero.

C = m + sum(duration_weight(di))
      + sum(max(0, abs(step_i)-2) + gap_weight(gi), i >= 2)

There is no separate length header or tuple rank. A greater number of simple notes competes with fewer complicated notes in the same cost budget. Eight repeated one-beat notes cost eight; one 128-beat note costs twenty-nine.

Visit costs in ascending order. Within a cost, visit the first duration in its existing duration-index order. For each later note, visit pitch steps in order 0,+1,-1,+2,-2,..., then the gap (zero first, then positive duration-index order), then its duration in duration-index order, then the next note. Only choices with a completion at the remaining cost occupy a block. End the phrase when no cost remains. The first note never has a pitch step or gap.

Every cost layer is finite, every tune has a finite positive cost, and each canonical tune occurs in one block exactly once. Consecutive indices over those blocks therefore give a bijection with nonnegative integers.

items.title: Rational counting and inversion
items.text:
Use rational generating functions for all counting tables, including duration counts and cumulative layer counts. Let D(z) count durations by their weight. For the default weights it is:

D(z) = (1-z^5)(1+z^3+z^4) / ((1-z)(1-2z^4)(1+z^4))

More generally, with x=z^BINARY_COST, t=z^NUMERATOR_COST, and s=z^THIRD_COST, it is (1-xt)(1+t+s)/((1-x)(1-2t)(1+t)). The numerator filters count reduced fractions, including the numerator one. For the default attack, step, and rest costs of one, define:

P(z) = 5+2z/(1-z)        # five free steps, then two at each positive cost
G(z) = 1+z*D(z)           # zero or positive gap
H(z) = 1/(1-z*D(z)*P(z)*G(z))
T(z) = z*D(z)*H(z)       # nonempty tunes

The completion series are H after a duration, D*H after a gap, and G*D*H after a step. Strictly preceding layer counts are coefficients of z*T/(1-z); preceding duration layers use z*D/(1-z). All are rational. Expand each N/Q with Q[0]=1 using the fixed linear recurrence:

coefficient[c] = N[c] - sum(Q[j]*coefficient[c-j], j >= 1)

Cache these exact big-integer tables. Find the tune's cost by binary search in the cumulative table, then subtract completion-count blocks for each component. Within a duration weight, select its reduced numerator by the existing exact group counts and binary search. Ranking sums the same preceding blocks. Neither direction visits previously enumerated tunes.

The six positive integer weights and free-step radius (two semitones) live together in nmr/types/tune_count.py. With radius k and tail step cost s, the pitch function is (2k+1)+2z^s/(1-z^s). Free steps form a finite set; the positive attack cost still keeps each complexity layer finite. They are design constants, not runtime settings. Changing them or the within-cost order changes truenames. Do not keep an old/new enumeration toggle or infer which scheme a truename used. Freeze the selected constants before release.

Initial tune indices (independent of the word vocabulary):

items.title: Rendering and playback
items.text:
Count's score represents the full-index tune that its truename button plays, which can differ from the prefix-relative tune in the description. Exact durations are split at barlines into notes, rests, dots, ties, and explicit tuplets. The score is shown one octave above playback in treble clef. Meter affects engraving only. nmr/web/music_notation.py generates this plan; VexFlow renders it locally through nmr/web/music-notation.mjs.

Each rendered symbol has a beat interval. Playback highlighting uses the audio context's elapsed time, converted at the playback tempo, to select the current symbol. It continues through rests and tied segments and clears on stop or tune completion. Count exposes an enable checkbox and a color picker, with green as the default. The tests check timing and SVG selection separately; these checks do not establish audible synchronization in a live browser.

class Main(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    operation: Literal["encode", "decode", "browse", "build-web"] = "decode"
    """Canonical decode is the default; browsing must be explicitly selected."""
    value: str | None = None
    """One input value. Omit to read one value per line from stdin or interactively."""
    type_name: Annotated[str | None, tyro.conf.arg(name="type")] = None
    """Type name, optionally qualified by parent categories; required for encoding."""
    scope: str | None = None
    """Encoding prefix scope. Default: type name. Empty string: no prefix."""
    word_file: Path | None = None
    word_count: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=1)
    case_sensitive: bool = False
    center_on_zoot: bool = True
    """Center Date and DateTime on 2027-01-01 00:00:00 UTC."""
    expect_vocabulary: str | None = None
    json_output: bool = False
    list_types: bool = False
    vocabulary_info: bool = False
    export_words: Path | None = None
    destination: Path = Path("dist/web")
    """Directory for --operation build-web; serve its static files over HTTP."""

    def run(self, source: TextIO, output: TextIO, errors: TextIO) -> int:
        if self.operation == "build-web":
            from .browser_build import build_browser

            print(build_browser(self.destination), file=output)
            return 0
        engine = Nmr(
            self.word_file,
            self.word_count,
            not self.case_sensitive,
            center_on_zoot=self.center_on_zoot,
        )
        if self.list_types:
            for path, description in engine.types().items():
                print(f"{path.rsplit(':', 1)[-1]}\t{description}", file=output)
            return 0
        if self.vocabulary_info:
            print(
                json.dumps(
                    {
                        "identifier": engine.identifier,
                        "words": engine.count,
                        "maximum_payload_words": engine.count,
                    }
                ),
                file=output,
            )
            return 0
        if self.export_words is not None:
            self.export_words.write_bytes(engine.export().encode())
            return 0
        if self.operation == "encode" and self.type_name is None:
            raise ValueError("Encoding requires --type")
        status = 0
        interactive = self.value is None and source.isatty()
        while True:
            if self.value is not None:
                value = self.value
            else:
                if interactive:
                    print("In: ", end="", file=errors, flush=True)
                if not (line := source.readline()):
                    break
                value = line.removesuffix("\n").removesuffix("\r")
            try:
                if self.operation == "encode":
                    result = engine.encode(value, self.type_name or "", self.scope)
                else:
                    result = engine.decode(
                        value, self.operation == "browse", self.expect_vocabulary
                    )
            except ValueError as error:
                print(f"ERROR: {error}", file=errors)
                status = 1
            else:
                if self.json_output:
                    print(result.model_dump_json(), file=output)
                else:
                    print(
                        result.truename if self.operation == "encode" else result.value,
                        file=output,
                    )
                    if self.operation == "browse":
                        print(f"Canonical truename: {result.truename}", file=errors)
            if self.value is not None:
                break
        return status

def build_browser(destination: Path, base_path: str = "./") -> Path:
    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    package = Path(__file__).parent
    sources = sorted(i for i in (package / "web").iterdir() if i.is_file())
    for source in sources:
        copyfile(source, destination / source.name)
    page = destination / "index.html"
    page.write_text(
        page.read_text().replace('<base href="./"', f'<base href="{escape(base_path)}"')
    )
    archive_path = destination / "python.zip"
    with ZipFile(archive_path, "w", compression=ZIP_DEFLATED) as archive:
        for name, distribution_name in [
            ("nmr", "nmr"),
            ("chess", "chess"),
            ("semver", "semver"),
            ("phonenumbers", "phonenumberslite"),
        ]:
            spec = util.find_spec(name)
            if spec is None or spec.origin is None:
                raise ValueError(f"Missing browser dependency: {name}")
            root = Path(spec.origin).parent
            for source in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
                if source.is_file() and (
                    source.suffix == ".py" or source == package / "words.txt"
                ):
                    archive.write(source, Path(name) / source.relative_to(root))
            distribution = metadata.distribution(distribution_name)
            for entry in distribution.files or []:
                if "license" in entry.name.lower() or "copying" in entry.name.lower():
                    archive.write(
                        str(distribution.locate_file(entry)),
                        Path("licenses") / name / entry.name,
                    )
    assets = [destination / i.name for i in sources]
    digest = sha256(archive_path.read_bytes())
    for asset in assets:
        digest.update(asset.name.encode())
        digest.update(asset.read_bytes())
    revision = digest.hexdigest()[:16]
    for asset in assets:
        if asset.suffix not in {".html", ".js", ".mjs"}:
            continue
        text = asset.read_text()
        for reference in [*assets, archive_path]:
            for prefix in ["", "./"]:
                path = prefix + reference.name
                text = text.replace(f'"{path}"', f'"{path}?v={revision}"')
        asset.write_text(text)
    return destination / "index.html"

class Category(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    name: str
    children: tuple[Category | type[TypeNamer], ...]

    def __init__(self, name: str, *children: Category | type[TypeNamer]) -> None:
        super().__init__(name=name, children=children)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_children(self) -> Category:
        if not 1 <= len(self.children) <= RADIX:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Child count {len(self.children)} is out of range 1..{RADIX}"
            )
        if len(self.children) == RADIX and not isinstance(self.children[-1], Category):
            raise ValueError("The last slot can never be a leaf")
        if any(isinstance(i, Category) and not i.name for i in self.children):
            raise ValueError("The unnamed root cannot be nested inside a category")
        labels = [label(i) for i in self.children]
        if len(labels) != len(set(labels)):
            raise ValueError("Sibling names must be unique")
        return self

    def leaves(
        self, prefix: str = ""
    ) -> Iterator[tuple[str, list[int], type[TypeNamer]]]:
        for path, slots, node in self.nodes(prefix):
            if not isinstance(node, Category):
                yield path, slots, node

    def nodes(
        self, prefix: str = ""
    ) -> Iterator[tuple[str, list[int], Category | type[TypeNamer]]]:
        for slot, child in enumerate(self.children):
            path = f"{prefix}{label(child)}"
            yield path, [slot], child
            if isinstance(child, Category):
                for name, slots, node in child.nodes(path + ":"):
                    yield name, [slot, *slots], node

    def lookup(self, path: str) -> tuple[Category | type[TypeNamer], list[int]]:
        if not path:
            return self, []
        path = path.removeprefix(":")
        matches = [
            (n, s) for p, s, n in self.nodes() if p == path or p.endswith(":" + path)
        ]
        # Bare time names the leaf; real:time still addresses its category.
        if path == "time" and len(matches) > 1:
            matches = [(n, s) for n, s in matches if not isinstance(n, Category)]
        if len(matches) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown or ambiguous category or type: {path}")
        node, slots = matches[0]
        return node, slots

    def resolve(self, index: int, browse: bool = False) -> tuple[type[TypeNamer], int]:
        if index < 0:
            raise ValueError("Expected a nonnegative index")
        node: Category | type[TypeNamer] = self
        while isinstance(node, Category):
            index, slot = divmod(index, RADIX)
            if slot >= len(node.children):
                if not browse:
                    raise ValueError("Truename selects an unassigned category slot")
                slot %= len(node.children)
            node = node.children[slot]
        return node, index

    model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)

    return index

class CountWords:
    def __init__(self, n: int) -> None:
        self.n = n
        self._perm_count = [(1, 0)]
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def count(self, c: int | None = None) -> int:
        if c is None:
            c = self.n

        if len(self._perm_count) - 1 < c:
            with self._lock:
                perm, count = self._perm_count[-1]

                for i in range(len(self._perm_count) - 1, c):
                    perm *= self.n - i
                    count += perm
                    self._perm_count.append((perm, count))

        return self._perm_count[c][1]

class Nmr(Words):
    def __init__(
        self,
        words: Sequence[str] | Path | None = None,
        count: int | None = None,
        ignore_case: bool = True,
        root: Category = ROOT,
        center_on_zoot: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(words, count, ignore_case)
        self.root = root
        self.center_on_zoot = center_on_zoot

    def types(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        return {p: c.description for p, _, c in self.root.leaves()}

    def encode(self, value: str, type_name: str, scope: str | None = None) -> Result:

class Packer(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    count: int = Field(ge=1)

    def pack(self, *numbers: int) -> int:
        if len(numbers) != self.count or any(i < 0 for i in numbers):
            raise ValueError(f"Expected {self.count} nonnegative integers")
        total = 0
        tail = 0
        for size, value in enumerate(reversed(numbers), 1):
            tail += value
            total += comb(tail + size - 1, size)
        return total

    def unpack(self, n: int) -> list[int]:
        if n < 0:
            raise ValueError("Expected a nonnegative integer")
        if self.count == 1:
            return [n]
        sums = []
        # comb(b, k) >= (b/k)**k gives an integer-only initial upper bound.
        upper = self.count * (1 << ((n.bit_length() + self.count - 1) // self.count))
        for size in range(self.count, 2, -1):
            lower = size - 1
            while upper - lower > 1:
                middle = (lower + upper) // 2
                if comb(middle, size) <= n:
                    lower = middle
                else:
                    upper = middle
            sums.append(lower - size + 1)
            n -= comb(lower, size)
            # The next binomial's upper argument must be smaller than this one.
            upper = lower
        first, last = unpair(n)
        sums.extend([first + last, last, 0])
        return [i - j for i, j in pairwise(sums)]

def to_truename(self, num: int) -> list[str]:
    if num < 0:
        raise ValueError("Only accepts non-negative numbers")
    length = next(
        (i for i in range(1, self.count + 1) if self.count_words(i) > num), None
    )
    if length is None:
        raise ValueError("Vocabulary capacity exceeded; choose a larger word list")
    total = num - self.count_words(length - 1)
    digits: list[int] = []
    used: list[int] = []
    for i in range(length):
        total, digit = divmod(total, self.count - i)
        for index in used:
            digit += index <= digit
        bisect.insort(used, digit)
        digits.append(digit)
    return [self.words[i] for i in reversed(digits)]

def from_truename(self, truename: Sequence[str]) -> int:
    words = [self.normalize(i) for i in truename]
    if not words:
        raise ValueError("A truename needs at least one word")
    if len(words) != len(set(words)):
        raise ValueError("A truename cannot repeat words")
    unknown = [i for i in words if i not in self.inverse]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError("Unrecognized words: " + ", ".join(unknown))
    indexes = [self.inverse[i] for i in reversed(words)]
    digits = [n - sum(i < n for i in indexes[:j]) for j, n in enumerate(indexes)]
    total = 0
    for i, digit in enumerate(reversed(digits)):
        total = total * (self.count - len(digits) + i + 1) + digit
    return self.count_words(len(words) - 1) + total

class Cards(TypeNamer):
    label = "cards"
    description = "52-card deck: changed-position cycles such as (1 2); () is ordered"

    @staticmethod
    def str_to_index(value: str) -> int:
        value = value.strip()
        permutation = list(range(DECK_SIZE))
        if re.fullmatch(r"\(\s*\)", value):
            return 0
        cycles = re.findall(r"\(([^()]*)\)", value)
        if not cycles or re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)", "", value).strip():
            raise ValueError("Use () or changed-position cycles such as (1 2)")
        used: set[int] = set()
        for cycle in cycles:
            tokens = cycle.split()
            if len(tokens) < 2 or any(not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", i) for i in tokens):
                raise ValueError("Each cycle needs at least two numbered positions")
            positions = [int(i) - 1 for i in tokens]
            for position in positions:
                if not 0 <= position < DECK_SIZE or position in used:
                    raise ValueError("Positions must be distinct numbers from 1 to 52")
                used.add(position)
            for origin, destination in zip(
                positions, positions[1:] + positions[:1], strict=True
            ):
                permutation[origin] = destination
        return rank_permutation(permutation)

    @staticmethod
    def index_to_str(index: int, browse: bool = False) -> str:
        permutation = unrank_permutation(bounded(index, DECK_COUNT, browse), DECK_SIZE)
        cycles = []
        used: set[int] = set()
        for origin, destination in enumerate(permutation):
            if origin == destination or origin in used:
                continue
            cycle = []
            position = origin
            while position not in used:
                used.add(position)
                cycle.append(position + 1)
                position = permutation[position]
            cycles.append("(" + " ".join(str(i) for i in cycle) + ")")
        return " ".join(cycles) or "()"

def rank_permutation(permutation: list[int]) -> int:
    """Rank by displaced count, lexicographic displaced subset, then images."""
    size = len(permutation)
    if sorted(permutation) != list(range(size)):
        raise ValueError("Expected a permutation of 0 through size minus one")
    positions = [i for i, n in enumerate(permutation) if i != n]
    moved = len(positions)
    offset = sum(comb(size, i) * completions(i, i) for i in range(moved))
    subset_rank = 0
    previous = -1
    for i, position in enumerate(positions):
        for candidate in range(previous + 1, position):
            subset_rank += comb(size - candidate - 1, moved - i - 1)
        previous = position
    remaining = set(positions)
    future = set(positions)
    forbidden = moved
    arrangement_rank = 0
    for position in positions:
        future.remove(position)
        for card in sorted(remaining):
            if card == position:
                continue
            next_forbidden = forbidden - (position in remaining) - (card in future)
            if card == permutation[position]:
                remaining.remove(card)
                forbidden = next_forbidden
                break
            arrangement_rank += completions(len(remaining) - 1, next_forbidden)
    return offset + subset_rank * completions(moved, moved) + arrangement_rank

def unrank_permutation(index: int, size: int) -> list[int]:
    """Invert rank_permutation by skipping counted subsets and image prefixes."""
    index = bounded(index, factorial(size), False)
    moved = 0
    while index >= (count := comb(size, moved) * completions(moved, moved)):
        index -= count
        moved += 1
    subset_rank, arrangement_rank = divmod(index, completions(moved, moved))
    positions = []
    candidate = 0
    for remaining_positions in range(moved, 0, -1):
        for position in range(candidate, size):
            count = comb(size - position - 1, remaining_positions - 1)
            if subset_rank >= count:
                subset_rank -= count
            else:
                positions.append(position)
                candidate = position + 1
                break
    permutation = list(range(size))
    remaining = set(positions)
    future = set(positions)
    forbidden = moved
    for position in positions:
        future.remove(position)
        for card in sorted(remaining):
            if card == position:
                continue
            next_forbidden = forbidden - (position in remaining) - (card in future)
            count = completions(len(remaining) - 1, next_forbidden)
            if arrangement_rank >= count:
                arrangement_rank -= count
            else:
                permutation[position] = card
                remaining.remove(card)
                forbidden = next_forbidden
                break
    return permutation

class GoBoard:
    """Alternating play, no suicide, situational superko, two passes end play.

    Legal moves are ordered A1, B1, ..., A2, ... with pass last. Board states
    include the next player for repetition checks. Passing is always legal
    before termination, even when it repeats a state.
    """

    def __init__(self, size: int) -> None:
        self.size = size
        self.stones = bytes(size * size)
        self.turn = 1
        self.passes = 0
        self.history = {(self.stones, self.turn)}
        self.neighbors = []
        for point in range(size * size):
            row, column = divmod(point, size)
            self.neighbors.append(
                [
                    r * size + c
                    for r, c in [
                        (row - 1, column),
                        (row + 1, column),
                        (row, column - 1),
                        (row, column + 1),
                    ]
                    if 0 <= r < size and 0 <= c < size
                ]
            )

    def parse_move(self, token: str) -> int:
        if token.casefold() == "pass":
            return self.size * self.size
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-HJ-T][1-9][0-9]?", token.upper()):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid Go coordinate: {token}")
        column = COLUMNS.index(token[0].upper())
        row = int(token[1:]) - 1
        if column >= self.size or row >= self.size:
            raise ValueError(f"Go coordinate outside the board: {token}")
        return row * self.size + column

    def format_move(self, move: int) -> str:
        if move == self.size * self.size:
            return "pass"
        row, column = divmod(move, self.size)
        return f"{COLUMNS[column]}{row + 1}"

    def legal_moves(self) -> dict[int, bytes]:
        if self.passes == 2:
            return {}
        moves = {}
        for point, stone in enumerate(self.stones):
            if stone:
                continue
            stones = bytearray(self.stones)
            stones[point] = self.turn
            for neighbor in self.neighbors[point]:
                if stones[neighbor] == 3 - self.turn:
                    group, liberties = self._group(stones, neighbor)
                    if not liberties:
                        for captured in group:
                            stones[captured] = 0
            _, liberties = self._group(stones, point)
            state = bytes(stones)
            if liberties and (state, 3 - self.turn) not in self.history:
                moves[point] = state
        moves[self.size * self.size] = self.stones
        return moves

    def play(self, move: int, stones: bytes) -> None:
        """Apply a move and resulting state from legal_moves()."""
        self.passes = self.passes + 1 if move == self.size * self.size else 0
        self.stones = stones
        self.turn = 3 - self.turn
        self.history.add((stones, self.turn))

    def _group(self, stones: bytearray, point: int) -> tuple[set[int], bool]:
        group = {point}
        pending = [point]
        liberties = False
        while pending:
            for neighbor in self.neighbors[pending.pop()]:
                if not stones[neighbor]:
                    liberties = True
                elif stones[neighbor] == stones[point] and neighbor not in group:
                    group.add(neighbor)
                    pending.append(neighbor)
        return group, liberties

class LatLong(TypeNamer):
    label = "latlong"
    description = (
        "Latitude,longitude in decimal degrees, rounded to a sub-metre cube grid"
    )

    @staticmethod
    def str_to_index(value: str) -> int:
        parts = value.split(",")
        if len(parts) != 2:
            raise ValueError("Expected latitude,longitude in decimal degrees")
        latitude, longitude = (float(i) for i in parts)
        if not -90 <= latitude <= 90 or not -180 <= longitude <= 180:
            raise ValueError("Latitude or longitude outside Earth coordinates")
        latitude, longitude = math.radians(latitude), math.radians(longitude)
        vector = (
            math.cos(latitude) * math.cos(longitude),
            math.cos(latitude) * math.sin(longitude),
            math.sin(latitude),
        )
        maximum = max(abs(i) for i in vector)
        # Fixed X/Y/Z priority also resolves floating-point noise at exact seams.
        axis = next(i for i in range(3) if abs(vector[i]) >= maximum - FACE_TOLERANCE)
        face = FACES.index((axis, 1 if vector[axis] >= 0 else -1))
        a, b = (
            coordinate_rank(vector[i] / abs(vector[axis]))
            for i in range(3)
            if i != axis
        )
        pair = a * a + b if a >= b else b * b + b + 1 + a
        return 6 * pair + face

    @staticmethod
    def index_to_str(index: int, browse: bool = False) -> str:
        index = bounded(index, SIZE, browse)
        pair, face = divmod(index, 6)
        shell = math.isqrt(pair)
        offset = pair - shell * shell
        a, b = (shell, offset) if offset <= shell else (offset - shell - 1, shell)
        axis, sign = FACES[face]
        vector = [coordinate_value(a), coordinate_value(b)]
        vector.insert(axis, float(sign))
        x, y, z = vector
        latitude = math.degrees(math.atan2(z, math.hypot(x, y)))
        longitude = (math.degrees(math.atan2(y, x)) + 180) % 360 - 180
        parts = [f"{i:.9f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".") for i in (latitude, longitude)]
        return ",".join("0" if i == "-0" else i for i in parts)

def coordinate_rank(value: float) -> int:
    """Round to an interior grid point, then rank it in midpoint-first order."""
    point = max(1, min(DIVISIONS - 1, math.floor((value + 1) * (DIVISIONS // 2) + 0.5)))
    shift = (point & -point).bit_length() - 1
    level = LEVELS - shift - 1
    return (1 << level) - 1 + ((point >> shift) - 1) // 2

def coordinate_value(rank: int) -> float:

class Tune(BaseModel, TypeNamer, frozen=True):
    notes: list[Note] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=256)
    label: ClassVar[str] = "tune"
    description: ClassVar[str] = "Melody and rhythm: @1 2@1/2 r@1/3 -1@2/3"

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_phrase(self) -> Tune:
        if self.notes[0].step or self.notes[0].gap:
            raise ValueError("The first note must have zero relative pitch and no gap")
        return self

    @classmethod
    def from_text(cls, value: str) -> Tune:
        if len(value) > MAX_TEXT:
            raise ValueError("Tune work limit: at most 20000 input characters")
        tokens = value.split()
        if not tokens or not tokens[0].startswith("@"):
            raise ValueError("A tune must start with @duration, without an offset")
        notes: list[Note] = []
        gap = Fraction(0)
        for token in tokens:
            match = re.fullmatch(r"(r|-?[0-9]*)@([0-9]+(?:/[0-9]+|\.[0-9]+)?)", token)
            if match is None:
                raise ValueError(f"Expected step@duration or r@duration: {token}")
            step, text = match.groups()
            if len(text) > MAX_WEIGHT:
                raise ValueError("Tune work limit: duration text is too large")
            try:
                duration = Fraction(text)
            except ZeroDivisionError as error:
                raise ValueError("A duration cannot have a zero denominator") from error
            duration_parts(duration)
            if step == "r":
                gap += duration
            else:
                notes.append(Note(step=int(step or "0"), duration=duration, gap=gap))
                gap = Fraction(0)
                if len(notes) > MAX_NOTES:
                    raise ValueError("Tune work limit: at most 256 attacked notes")
        # Trailing rests are outside the phrase, just as leading performance silence is.
        return cls(notes=notes)

    @classmethod
    def from_pitches(
        cls, pitches: list[int], durations: list[Fraction], gaps: list[Fraction]
    ) -> Tune:
        """Normalize absolute pitches and leading silence, retaining every attack."""
        if not pitches or len(pitches) != len(durations) or len(pitches) != len(gaps):
            raise ValueError(
                "Expected equally sized, nonempty pitch/duration/gap lists"
            )
        return cls(
            notes=[
                Note(
                    step=p - pitches[i - 1] if i else 0,
                    duration=d,
                    gap=g if i else Fraction(0),
                )
                for i, (p, d, g) in enumerate(
                    zip(pitches, durations, gaps, strict=True)
                )
            ]
        )

    def text(self) -> str:
        tokens = []
        for note in self.notes:
            if note.gap:
                tokens.append(f"r@{note.gap}")
            tokens.append(f"{note.step or ''}@{note.duration}")
        return " ".join(tokens)

    def index(self) -> int:
        cost = len(self.notes) * tune_count.ATTACK_COST
        cost += sum(duration_cost(i.duration) for i in self.notes)
        cost += sum(
            tune_count.pitch_cost(i.step) + gap_cost(i.gap) for i in self.notes[1:]
        )
        if cost > MAX_COST:
            raise ValueError("Tune work limit: total complexity exceeds 4096")
        tables = tune_count.tune_counts(MAX_COST)
        remaining = cost - tune_count.ATTACK_COST
        rank, remaining = rank_duration(
            self.notes[0].duration, remaining, tables["suffix"], sounding=True
        )
        for note in self.notes[1:]:
            remaining -= tune_count.ATTACK_COST
            # Pitch order is 0,+1,-1,+2,-2,... within the remaining budget.
            for i in range(signed_index(note.step)):
                weight = tune_count.pitch_cost(signed_value(i))
                rank += tables["after_step"][remaining - weight]
            remaining -= tune_count.pitch_cost(note.step)
            if note.gap:
                rank += tables["after_gap"][remaining]
                addition, remaining = rank_duration(
                    note.gap, remaining - tune_count.REST_COST, tables["after_gap"]
                )
                rank += addition
            addition, remaining = rank_duration(
                note.duration, remaining, tables["suffix"], sounding=True
            )
            rank += addition
        assert remaining == 0
        index = tables["starts"][cost] + rank
        check_index(index)
        return index

    def tie(self, index: int) -> Tune:
        """Replace two contiguous same-pitch notes with one sustained note."""
        if not 1 <= index < len(self.notes):
            raise ValueError("Choose a later note to tie to its predecessor")
        note, previous = self.notes[index], self.notes[index - 1]
        if note.step or note.gap:
            raise ValueError("Tied notes must share a pitch with no intervening gap")
        sustained = Note(
            step=previous.step,
            duration=previous.duration + note.duration,
            gap=previous.gap,
        )
        return Tune(
            notes=[*self.notes[: index - 1], sustained, *self.notes[index + 1 :]]
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_index(cls, index: int) -> Tune:
        check_index(index)
        tables = tune_count.tune_counts(MAX_COST)
        if index >= tables["starts"][-1]:
            raise ValueError("Tune work limit: total complexity exceeds 4096")
        cost = bisect_right(tables["starts"], index) - 1
        rank = index - tables["starts"][cost]
        duration, rank, remaining = unrank_duration(
            rank, cost - tune_count.ATTACK_COST, tables["suffix"], sounding=True
        )
        notes = [Note(duration=duration)]
        while remaining:
            if len(notes) >= MAX_NOTES:
                raise ValueError("Tune work limit: at most 256 attacked notes")
            remaining -= tune_count.ATTACK_COST
            for step_index in range(
                2 * (tune_count.FREE_STEPS + remaining // tune_count.STEP_COST) + 1
            ):
                step = signed_value(step_index)
                weight = tune_count.pitch_cost(step)
                count = (
                    tables["after_step"][remaining - weight]
                    if weight <= remaining
                    else 0
                )
                if rank < count:
                    remaining -= weight
                    break
                rank -= count
            else:
                raise AssertionError("Pitch completion count is inconsistent")
            count = tables["after_gap"][remaining]
            gap = Fraction(0)
            if rank >= count:
                gap, rank, remaining = unrank_duration(
                    rank - count, remaining - tune_count.REST_COST, tables["after_gap"]
                )
            duration, rank, remaining = unrank_duration(
                rank, remaining, tables["suffix"], sounding=True
            )
            notes.append(Note(step=step, gap=gap, duration=duration))
        assert rank == 0
        return cls(notes=notes)

    def events(
        self, root: int = 60, position: Literal["start", "middle", "end"] = "middle"
    ) -> list[dict[str, int | str]]:
        """Exact onsets, durations and positioned MIDI pitches, before device limits."""
        pitches = []
        pitch = 0
        for note in self.notes:
            pitch += note.step
            pitches.append(pitch)
        if position == "start":
            center = pitches[0]
        elif position == "end":
            center = pitches[-1]
        elif position == "middle":
            total = sum(pitches)
            center = (2 * abs(total) + len(pitches)) // (2 * len(pitches))
            if total < 0:
                center = -center
        else:
            raise ValueError("Position must be start, middle, or end")
        onset = Fraction(0)
        events = []
        for note, pitch in zip(self.notes, pitches, strict=True):
            onset += note.gap
            events.append(
                {
                    "pitch": root + pitch - center,
                    "onset": str(onset),
                    "duration": str(note.duration),
                }
            )
            onset += note.duration
        return events

    def playback(
        self,
        root: int = 60,
        bpm: int = 120,
        position: Literal["start", "middle", "end"] = "middle",
    ) -> list[dict[str, float | int]]:
        """Convert exact events only after checking the browser's preview limits."""
        if not 20 <= bpm <= 400:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Playback tempo must be between 20 and 400 BPM; got {bpm} BPM"
            )
        events = self.events(root, position)
        result = []
        violations = []
        for number, event in enumerate(events, 1):
            pitch = int(event["pitch"])
            onset = Fraction(str(event["onset"])) * 60 / bpm
            duration = Fraction(str(event["duration"])) * 60 / bpm
            if not 0 <= pitch <= 127:
                violations.append(
                    f"note {number} positioned pitch is {pitch}; "
                    "allowed MIDI range is 0..127"
                )
            result.append(
                {"pitch": pitch, "onset": float(onset), "duration": float(duration)}
            )
        if violations:
            raise ValueError("Playback limit: " + "; ".join(violations))
        return result

    @staticmethod
    def str_to_index(value: str) -> int:
        return Tune.from_text(value).index()

    @staticmethod
    def index_to_str(index: int, browse: bool = False) -> str:
        return Tune.from_index(index).text()

def unrank_duration(
    rank: int, budget: int, completions: list[int], sounding: bool = False
) -> tuple[Fraction, int, int]:
    tables = tune_count.tune_counts(MAX_COST)
    kind = "note_duration" if sounding else "duration"
    for weight in range(budget + 1):
        suffixes = completions[budget - weight]
        count = tables[kind][weight] * suffixes
        if rank >= count:
            rank -= count
            continue
        ordinal, rank = divmod(rank, suffixes)
        if weight > MAX_WEIGHT:
            raise ValueError("Tune work limit: duration weight exceeds 512")
        return (
            duration_value(tables[kind + "_starts"][weight] + ordinal, sounding),
            rank,
            budget - weight,
        )

def duration_parts(value: Fraction) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    if value <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Durations must be positive")
    denominator = value.denominator
    a = (denominator & -denominator).bit_length() - 1
    denominator >>= a
    b = int(denominator % 3 == 0)
    if denominator != 3**b:
        raise ValueError(
            "Reduced denominators allow only powers of two "
            "and at most one factor of three"
        )
    u = value.numerator
    h = u.bit_length() - 1
    if (
        tune_count.NUMERATOR_COST * h
        + tune_count.BINARY_COST * a
        + tune_count.THIRD_COST * b
        > MAX_WEIGHT
    ):
        raise ValueError("Tune work limit: duration weight exceeds 512")
    return u, a, b, h

def coefficients(numerator: list[int], denominator: list[int], limit: int) -> list[int]:
    """Expand N/Q using Q[0] = 1, with fixed work per coefficient."""
    if denominator[0] != 1:
        raise ValueError("The rational denominator must have constant term one")
    result: list[int] = []
    for cost in range(limit + 1):
        value = numerator[cost] if cost < len(numerator) else 0
        value -= sum(
            denominator[i] * result[cost - i]
            for i in range(1, min(cost + 1, len(denominator)))
        )
        result.append(value)
    return result

def duration_function() -> tuple[list[int], list[int]]:
    """D = (1-xt)(1+t+s) / ((1-x)(1-2t)(1+t)).

    Here x=z**BINARY_COST, t=z**NUMERATOR_COST, s=z**THIRD_COST.
    Counts reduced numerators only, including the exceptional numerator one.
    """
    numerator = polynomial_product(
        polynomial_sum([1], power(BINARY_COST + NUMERATOR_COST, -1)),
        polynomial_sum([1], power(NUMERATOR_COST), power(THIRD_COST)),
    )
    denominator = polynomial_product(
        polynomial_sum([1], power(BINARY_COST, -1)),
        polynomial_sum([1], power(NUMERATOR_COST, -2)),
        polynomial_sum([1], power(NUMERATOR_COST)),
    )
    return numerator, denominator

def note_duration_function() -> tuple[list[int], list[int]]:
    """Remove durations below 1/24 beat from the unrestricted duration series.

    For numerator bit length h+1, binary durations below the cutoff have
    denominator exponent h+5 (partially) or >=h+6 (entirely). Durations with
    a factor of three are excluded at exponents >=h+4.
    With t=z**(NUMERATOR_COST+BINARY_COST), the respective numerator counts
    have series C=(1-t-t²)/((1-2t)(1+t)), A=(1-t)/(1-2t),
    and B=(1-t)/((1-2t)(1+t)).
    """
    n, q = duration_function()
    diagonal = NUMERATOR_COST + BINARY_COST
    binary_q = polynomial_sum([1], power(BINARY_COST, -1))
    removed_q = polynomial_product(
        binary_q,
        polynomial_sum([1], power(diagonal, -2)),
        polynomial_sum([1], power(diagonal)),
    )
    removed_n = polynomial_sum(
        polynomial_product(
            power(5 * BINARY_COST),
            binary_q,
            polynomial_sum([1], power(diagonal, -1), power(2 * diagonal, -1)),
        ),
        polynomial_product(
            power(6 * BINARY_COST),
            polynomial_sum([1], power(2 * diagonal, -1)),
        ),
        polynomial_product(
            power(4 * BINARY_COST + THIRD_COST),
            polynomial_sum([1], power(diagonal, -1)),
        ),
    )
    numerator = polynomial_sum(
        polynomial_product(n, removed_q),
        [-i for i in polynomial_product(removed_n, q)],
    )
    return numerator, polynomial_product(q, removed_q)

Count completions at each stage, all by rational series recurrences.

D=N/Q counts gaps, M/R counts sounding durations >=1/24 beat. P=(2FREE_STEPS+1)+2zSTEP_COST/(1-zSTEP_COST). G=1+z**REST_COST*D. H=1/(1-z**ATTACK_COSTM/RPG) counts possibly empty note suffixes. The three completion series are H, M/RH and GM/RH.

@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def tune_counts(limit: int) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
    """Count completions at each stage, all by rational series recurrences.

    D=N/Q counts gaps, M/R counts sounding durations >=1/24 beat.
    P=(2*FREE_STEPS+1)+2*z**STEP_COST/(1-z**STEP_COST).
    G=1+z**REST_COST*D.
    H=1/(1-z**ATTACK_COST*M/R*P*G) counts possibly empty note suffixes.
    The three completion series are H, M/R*H and G*M/R*H.
    """
    n, q = duration_function()
    m, r = note_duration_function()
    pitch_n = polynomial_sum([2 * FREE_STEPS + 1], power(STEP_COST, 1 - 2 * FREE_STEPS))
    pitch_q = polynomial_sum([1], power(STEP_COST, -1))
    gap_n = polynomial_sum(q, polynomial_product(power(REST_COST), n))
    suffix_n = polynomial_product(r, q, pitch_q)
    denominator = polynomial_sum(
        suffix_n,
        polynomial_product(power(ATTACK_COST, -1), m, pitch_n, gap_n),
    )
    tables = {
        "duration": coefficients(n, q, limit),
        "note_duration": coefficients(m, r, limit),
        "suffix": coefficients(suffix_n, denominator, limit),
        "after_gap": coefficients(
            polynomial_product(m, q, pitch_q), denominator, limit
        ),
        "after_step": coefficients(
            polynomial_product(m, pitch_q, gap_n), denominator, limit
        ),
    }
    # Strictly preceding layers: z*T/(1-z) and z*D/(1-z).
    cumulative_q = [1, -1]
    tables["starts"] = coefficients(
        polynomial_product(power(ATTACK_COST + 1), m, q, pitch_q),
        polynomial_product(denominator, cumulative_q),
        limit + 1,
    )
    tables["duration_starts"] = coefficients(
        polynomial_product(power(1), n),
        polynomial_product(q, cumulative_q),
        limit + 1,
    )
    tables["note_duration_starts"] = coefficients(
        polynomial_product(power(1), m),
        polynomial_product(r, cumulative_q),
        limit + 1,
    )
    return tables

def score_plan(
    tune: Tune,
    root: int,
    position: Literal["start", "middle", "end"],
    meter: TimeSignature,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Engrave playback events one octave higher without changing their timing.

    Preview limits bound the number of SVG elements, not the accepted meter.
    Unusually tiny durations use an explicit tuplet rather than rounding.
    """
    tune.playback(root=root, bpm=180, position=position)
    events = tune.events(root=root, position=position)
    measures: list[list[dict[str, object]]] = [[]]
    bar = Fraction(4 * meter.top, meter.bottom)
    cursor = Fraction(0)
    end = Fraction(0)
    count = 0
    for attack, event in enumerate(events):
        onset = Fraction(str(event["onset"]))
        spans = [
            (onset - end, None),
            (Fraction(str(event["duration"])), event["pitch"]),
        ]
        for duration, pitch in spans:
            continuation = False
            while duration:
                if cursor == bar:
                    measures.append([])
                    cursor = Fraction(0)
                if len(measures) > 512 or count >= 4096:
                    raise ValueError(
                        "This score exceeds the notation preview limit "
                        "(512 bars or 4096 symbols)."
                    )
                remaining = min(duration, bar - cursor)
                ratio = [3, 2] if remaining.denominator % 3 == 0 else [1, 1]
                written = remaining * Fraction(*ratio)
                candidates = [i for i in GLYPHS if i[0] <= written]
                if candidates:
                    length, glyph, dots = max(candidates)
                    actual = length / Fraction(*ratio)
                else:
                    glyph, dots = "128", 0
                    actual = remaining
                    multiplier = Fraction(1, 32) / actual
                    ratio = [multiplier.numerator, multiplier.denominator]
                    if max(ratio) > 1024:
                        raise ValueError(
                            "This score needs a tuplet ratio too large "
                            "for the notation preview."
                        )
                measures[-1].append(
                    {
                        "pitch": int(pitch) + 12 if pitch is not None else None,
                        "duration": str(actual),
                        "glyph": glyph,
                        "dots": dots,
                        "ratio": ratio,
                        "attack": attack if pitch is not None else None,
                        "tie": continuation,
                    }
                )
                continuation = pitch is not None
                duration -= actual
                cursor += actual
                count += 1
        end = onset + Fraction(str(event["duration"]))
    return {
        "top": str(meter.top),
        "bottom": meter.bottom,
        "clef": "treble",
        "measures": measures,
    }
